name: Hagia Sophia
desc: 1,500 years of empires arguing over the same dome. Stand under it once and your group chat will hear about it forever.

name: Blue Mosque
desc: Six minarets and a ceiling of blue tiles that will crane your neck the good way. Free — dress modest and drift in.

name: Topkapi Palace
desc: Sultans' quarters, emerald daggers and harem gossip fossilized in tile. Steep ticket, but it is basically time travel.

name: Grand Bazaar
desc: 4,000 shops of lamps, rugs and tea-fueled negotiation. Enter broke, leave broke but carrying excellent stories.

name: Spice Bazaar
desc: Pyramids of saffron, lokum and pepper perfume the air at no charge. Sniffing is on the house; willpower not included.

name: Galata Tower
desc: Medieval lookout with the postcard shot of the Golden Horn. Pricey lift, but sunset up here files firmly under someday-worthy.

name: Basilica Cistern
desc: An underground forest of columns with two Medusa heads doing headstands. Moody, drippy, gloriously weird.

name: Bosphorus Public Ferry
desc: Two continents, one glass of tea, a squad of seagulls — for about a dollar. The best cheap thrill in Istanbul, full stop.

name: Istiklal Street
desc: A red tram sliding through a river of three million people. Window-shop, snack, repeat — the city's free treadmill.

name: Süleymaniye Mosque
desc: Sinan's masterpiece on the third hill, quieter than the Blue Mosque with a skyline view thrown in free. Sit, breathe, plot your future.
